observations.title: Bounded regex on internal report-path strings
observations.technical_explanation: The regex ^relationshipEngine\[([^\]]+)\](?:\.(.*))?$ uses a single character-class negation for the bracket content and a single .* for the optional suffix. Neither sub-pattern has nested or overlapping quantifiers, so there is no catastrophic backtracking vector. The matched string originates from fixture report-path definitions within the project, not from untrusted or user-supplied input.
observations.layman_explanation: The flagged pattern is a straightforward string-matching expression with no dangerous complexity, and it only sees data defined inside the project itself.

observations.title: All five dynamic-execution candidates belong to the same test harness function
observations.technical_explanation: All five candidates are within the same test case named 'narration handoff display is optional routed and independently persistent' in the behavior test file. Each `new Function` call follows the identical pattern: read `index.js` from disk, slice out a function body by string boundary matching, wrap it in `new Function` with named parameter injection, and invoke with hardcoded test values. No candidate involves network access, credential handling, user input, or persistence. The test file imports `node:fs` and `node:assert/strict` and runs as a standalone Node script, not as part of the browser-loaded extension.
observations.layman_explanation: All five flagged code sections are part of the same test that checks how the extension's display widgets work. Each one simply extracts a piece of the extension's own code and tests it with fixed values. None of them handle user input, network traffic, or sensitive data.

observations.title: Test harness uses new Function to isolate and test widget geometry functions
observations.technical_explanation: The test reads `index.js` from the local filesystem, extracts a block of tracker widget geometry functions by string slicing between two known function declarations, and wraps them in `new Function` with named parameters for constants and mock globals. The mock document provides only a single querySelector that returns a fixed bounding rect. All test assertions use hardcoded numeric inputs and expected outputs. No network, credential, persistence, or user-input data flow is present.
observations.layman_explanation: This test checks that the extension's widget positioning math works correctly by pulling the relevant functions out of the extension's own code and testing them with fixed numbers. No outside data or sensitive information is involved.
